key_insight: PRIME adds a learned feedback loop to VLA driving models so early perception can be guided by what the system has already reasoned and planned. This helps the model focus on the most relevant visual cues instead of treating every frame the same way.
problem_solved: Standard VLA models process vision in a mostly feedforward way, so perception does not benefit from downstream goals, navigation context, or prior decisions. This can make the model overlook important cues that should be prioritized for driving decisions.
method: Introduces situational memory embeddings that carry task- and context-specific information back into the perception stage.
Uses a learned perception feedback mechanism to bias early visual processing toward cues relevant to reasoning and planning.
Integrates the feedback loop into VLA models for autonomous driving while preserving temporal recurrence in perception.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, PRIME shows a practical way to make multimodal driving models more goal-aware and context-sensitive. This can improve robustness, attention allocation, and decision quality in autonomous driving systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing perception → reasoning → planning with a feedback arrow back to perception
Memory embedding block illustrating situational context being stored and reused
Before/after comparison of feedforward vs PRIME-guided perception attention

paper_title: PRIME: Perception Feedback with Situational Memory Embeddings in VLA Models
paper_authors: Erik Deinzer, Naya Baslan, Luca Paparusso, Narunas Vaskevicius, Peter Knott
